questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Crack someone up

options.text: To force someone to commit a mistake

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'To make someone laugh'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word meaning of the given idiom is **'To make someone laugh'.**
 
• Explanation: The idiom** "crack someone up" **means to make someone laugh uncontrollably or to cause amusement. It originated from the idea of causing someone to burst into laughter, often with the implication that the laughter is sudden and intense, like the sound of something cracking.
 
• ***For example,**__ if someone tells a hilarious joke that makes another person laugh so hard that they can't stop, you could say, "That joke really **cracked him up.**"*
 
• The origin of the **idiom** is not definitively known, but it likely stems from the concept of "**cracking**" **someone's composure or seriousness, replacing it with laughter. **

questions.question:
**Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence.**

He really ***stinks and smells foul*** after a hard session at the gym.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **pen and ink**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase "**stinks and smells foul**" refers to a very unpleasant smell (बहुत बुरी तरह से बदबू आना).

 
 
• **Example**: After jogging in the park during summer, he **stinks and smells foul**.
 
 
 
• The correct idiomatic expression "**pen and ink**" is used to imply something that smells bad (बदबू).
 
 
• **Example**: When he removed his shoes, the whole room was filled with **pen and ink**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is **pen and ink**.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **An old flame:** Refers to a former lover or someone with whom one had a romantic relationship (पुराना प्यार).

 
 
• **Example**: During the high school reunion, he was surprised to see his old flame.
 
 
 
• **An iron will**: Means having a very strong determination or willpower (मजबूत इच्छाशक्ति).
 
 
• **Example**: Despite the challenges, she completed her degree with an iron will.
 
 
 
• **Lame excuse**: A weak or poor excuse for something, not convincing (कमजोर बहाना).
 
 
• **Example**: He gave a lame excuse for his absence, saying his alarm clock didn't ring.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Grasping at straws

options.text: Trying to find the best way to compete with others when nothing you choose is likely to work
Trying to find some way to succeed when you see others are also doing the same
Trying to find some way to succeed when nothing you choose is likely to work
Trying to find manipulative ways to succeed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 3".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Grasping at straws: **The idiom signifies a desperate attempt to find a solution or some hope when in a situation that seems hopeless or "Trying to find some way to succeed when nothing you choose is likely to work." (निराशा की स्थिति में किसी समाधान या आशा की तलाश).
 
• **Example: **After losing his job unexpectedly, John was **grasping at straws** to pay his monthly bills.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Trying to find some way to succeed when nothing you choose is likely to work."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Trying to find the best way to compete with others when nothing you choose is likely to work(प्रतिस्पर्धा पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना बजाय किसी भी समाधान की हताश खोज के).
 
• Trying to find some way to succeed when you see others are also doing the same:(हताश स्थिति के बजाय दूसरों की तरह सफलता के तरीके ढूंढना).
 
• Trying to find manipulative ways to succeed: This suggests using deceit or manipulation to achieve success, which is not conveyed by the idiom "grasping at straws" (सफलता प्राप्त करने के लिए छल या हेरफेर का इस्तेमाल करने का तात्पर्य, जो कि मुहावरे "grasping at straws" द्वारा व्यक्त नहीं किया जाता है).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Keep a straight face

options.text: Get on extremely well with someone
Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Keep a straight face:** This phrase refers to the act of maintaining a serious expression or not showing amusement in a situation where laughing or smiling might be the instinctive reaction. (बिना हँसे या अपना भाव बदले रखना)
 
• Correct Expression and Meaning: 'Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh' (बिना हँसे या अपना भाव बदले रहने का अर्थ है अपने चेहरे के भाव को नियंत्रित करना ताकि किसी मजाकिया स्थिति पर प्रतिक्रिया न दिखाई दे).
 
• **Example:** Despite the comic's hilarious jokes, she managed to **keep a straight face** throughout the performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Become very confused (बहुत भ्रमित होना): This suggests a state of perplexity or inability to understand something, which is not related to controlling one's facial expressions.
 
• Get on extremely well with someone (किसी के साथ बहुत अच्छे से मिलना-जुलना): This indicates a harmonious or very friendly relationship with another person, which again, has no connection to maintaining a neutral facial expression.
 
• Make more of an effort (अधिक प्रयास करना): This suggests trying harder in a general context, such as in work or personal endeavors, and does not specifically relate to the act of not showing laughter or amusement.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He got a __burst of energy__ and started digging again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 i.e. 'second wind'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase **"burst of energy"** refers to a sudden increase in energy or enthusiasm.

 
 
• **Example:** After resting for a while, the marathon runner got a burst of energy and was able to finish the race.
 
 
 
• The correct idiom **"second wind**" means finding new strength or energy to continue after becoming tired or discouraged. 
 
 
• **Example:** Just when I was about to give up on the project, I found my second wind and managed to complete it on time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is- Second wind.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Took bull by the horns" **means to confront a problem head-on.

 
 
• **Example**: He decided to take the bull by the horns and discuss his issues directly with his manager.
 
 
 
• **"A fancy of someone" **means something that someone likes very much or is very interested in. 
 
 
• **Example**: Collecting antique coins is a fancy of his; he's been at it for years.
 
 
 
• **"Heart on the sleeve" **means to openly show one's feelings or emotions. 
 
 
• **Example**: She always wears her heart on her sleeve, so you always know how she's feeling.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Steer clear of

options.text: Loose temper and react furiously to someone
Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you
Show someone how to do a job or activity
Be kind and empathetic to someone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"steer clear of"** means to avoid or stay away from something, often due to danger, trouble, or undesirable consequences.
 
• It implies an effort to keep a safe and cautious distance from a particular situation or person.
 
 
• **Example:** *After hearing about the recent issues at the company, Reena decided to **steer clear of **any involvement in office politics.*
 
 
 
• From the above example, it is clear that **"avoid some or something because it is dangerous for you"** is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **"Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you".**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some idioms that convey a similar meaning to **"Steer clear of"**:

 
 
• **Keep one's distance:** Stay away or avoid getting too close.

 
 
• Example: *It's wise to keep one's distance from any wild animal.*
 
 
 
• **Keep at arm's length:** To maintain a safe or cautious distance.
 
 
• Example: *Since going to college, he has kept his old friends at arm's length.*
 
 
 
• **Stay out of harm's way:** To avoid situations that could be dangerous or harmful.
 
 
• Example: *He asked the children to stay out of his arm's way while he made dinner.*

questions.question:

options.text: An absence of fear or anxiety
The capacity to maintain composure when stressed

questions.solution:

• **Example: **Despite the turbulence, the pilot, with** nerves of steel**, successfully landed the plane.
 
 
 
• **"The capacity to maintain composure when stressed"** refers to staying calm and collected under pressure. (तनाव में शांत रहना)

• **Relentless determination** (अविरल दृढ़ संकल्प): Unyielding or persistent determination.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get itchy feet

options.text: Learn something by memorising it without a thought to what is being learnt
To start to want to travel or do something different
Join a popular trend or activity

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Get itchy feet"** means to start to feel a strong desire to travel or move from one place to another. • **Example: **With mounting debts and no job, he felt like his **back was against the wall**.
 
 
 
• **"Difficult circumstance with no escape at all"** matches the meaning of the idiom "Back against the wall," indicating helplessness in a tough situation. (मुसीबत में फंसा हुआ)
 
 
• **Example:** The agents were stuck in a dangerous mission with no way out, making them feel like their **backs were against the wall**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **"Back against the wall"** is the most appropriate choice for the underlined segment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Back against the wall)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To give one a long rope** (किसी को स्वतंत्रता देना): To allow someone the freedom to act as they please, even if it might lead to trouble.

 
 
• **Example:** The manager decided **to give the new employee a long rope** to see how he handled responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **To go to the dogs** (बिगड़ जाना): To deteriorate or decline in quality, value, or success.
 
 
• **Example:** The business **went to the dogs** after the owner mismanaged it.
 
 
 
• **To give currency** (लोकप्रिय बनाना): To make something widely known or accepted.
 
 
• **Example:** The media **gave currency** to the rumour about the celebrity's secret wedding.
